chunks: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a Muslim who slaughtered a sheep and named (said Bismillah), but the knife, by its sharpness, outpaced him and severed the head. He (peace be upon him) said: If the blood flows out, then eat.

key_terms.بِحِدَّتِهَا: By its sharpness/severity — referring to the unintended excessive force or keenness of the blade
key_terms.خَرَجَ الدَّمُ: The blood flows out — the key condition for permissibility
key_terms.سَمَّى: Pronounced the name of God (Bismillah) at the moment of slaughter — an obligatory condition for halal slaughter
key_terms.فَأَبَانَ الرَّأْسَ: It severed/separated the head — a situation that could render the slaughter doubtful

ai.seo_question: Is the meat halal if the knife accidentally severs the head during slaughter after saying Bismillah?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) regarding an edge case in Islamic slaughter (dhabh): when a Muslim properly invokes God's name but the knife, due to its extreme sharpness, inadvertently severs the entire head. The Imam rules that if blood flows out normally, the meat is permissible to eat. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that the essential conditions — proper intention, invoking God's name, and effective blood flow — are the determinative factors of valid slaughter, even when the physical act exceeds what was intended.
